answer: Anchor each identity to a public history of useful work: to stay active, an agent must regularly complete tasks whose outputs other agents can check, and every result is recorded on-chain. A new identity starts with zero history, so it earns nothing until it has proven itself. The bridge between identity and income is this verifiable record, not a cheap registration form, so an attacker cloning a thousand fake agents must pay the full work cost a thousand times. Nectar, the rewards, flows only to identities with sustained, checked contributions, making mass forgery cost more than it earns.
